100 Yds.—1, Wigley (T); 2, Masters (P); 3, Bowers (BP) 4, Wright (BP).

The 880 yards saw Bob Taylor continue his good form by winning the race in 1 min. 57.3 secs. which equalled last year's time. "Jumbo" Masters also competed, but found the pace a little too fast for him, but will do better with more experience of such races.

Not far behind Chas. was "[illegible]umbo" Masters in 41st place, a good performance especially in view of his recent foot injury. Dennis Brickwood running in his usual steady manner, was our next man to finish coming 73rd.
The lead changed several times first Trower, then Masters. Short took over at 3 miles and then Maynard came through at about 4 miles and strolled home untroubled.
Bagnall and Walker ran well for 2nd and 3rd place, followed by the usual crowd with Masters having an easy run whipping up the end of our pack.
John Burr 5th, gave us a good start. 6th was Johnny Butley, first man home for Surrey A.C. and then four more Bels., Masters, Tooby Trower and Bagnall.

After the first half mile we had Masters, Walker and Bagnall in the first 20, with Patterson Baulch, Short, Trower and Bedford in the twenties, and although positions changed a bit, our scoring six were always placed well in the first thirty.

Bagnall was soon prominent, being third after half a mile, with Masters only a few places behind him. Foord of Brighton and Barrett, SAC. were first and second almost from the start and never looked as though they would be replaced.

At about 2½ miles Cliff was still leading our team and lying about 60th, Pete Bagnall was next, 83rd with Eddie Patterson 85th, next J. Masters 96th, Dave Baulch 118th, Charlie Walker 120th, Eric Gebbett about 150th, and Jack Brown about 160th.
Masters then pulled the "A" Team up to 4th place but Brian Trower showed his lack of recent racing with a rather slow time which contributed greatly to our subsequent defeat.
Masters "A", Abbott "B" and Jordon "V" went off first and Dave Abbot was seen in the lead after half a mile but unfortunately fell away badly in the second half of his run.

Knight of Essex Beagles was the individual winner completing the course in record time and finishing in front of Sando. Pete Bagnall was our first man home in 11th position and supported by Masters, Short and L. Bishop, we gained 3rd place in the team event.
Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.

Masters, despite the amount of training he puts in (often of the wrong type I fear) was most disappointing and must chabge his attitude of mind if he hopes to make the progress he showed a year or two ago.
4. · J. Masters

Jim Masters on the switchback course through Redhill and Earlswood again gave us hope by passing three clubs and taking us up to 6th. Thames Valley, however, were represented by Norris and added 10 more seconds to their lead.
Then followed a string of runners before we again saw a Belgrave vest filled by Eddie Short who had John Moore and Jumbo Masters close on his heels, all of them in the 130's.

Jim Masters took the fifth leg and remained in the same position, although losing ground on the teams ahead. Don Maclean who is in great form these days, went off last and with a good effort gained one place to bring us into fifth place.
Charlie Walker took over five seconds down on the Valley man and in the course of chasing and catching his quarry he passed three others to give 'Jumbo' Masters the baton, in fifth spot.

Sawyer showed a good turn of speed for a man who does "double marathon" stuff and maintained our position, but Masters, whose first race this was for 4 months because of injury, was forced to give a place on the run in for the final change-over.
